How Speak Up! works

Every unit follows the same 7 steps. Each step is based on research into how people really learn to speak a foreign language. Har bir bo‘lim 7 bosqichdan iborat. Har bir bosqich til o‘rganish bo‘yicha tadqiqotlarga asoslangan.

  1. 1
    Key phrases

    Fluent speakers use ready-made phrases. Learning phrases, not single words, lets you speak faster.

    Tayyor iboralar bilan tezroq gapirasiz.
  2. 2
    Listen & shadow

    Repeating after native audio trains pronunciation, rhythm and listening together.

    Audio ortidan takrorlash talaffuz va ritmni rivojlantiradi.
  3. 3
    Build it

    Short pattern drills make grammar automatic — no translating in your head.

    Qisqa mashqlar grammatikani avtomatik qiladi.
  4. 4
    Remember it

    Saying phrases from memory, again after 1 day and 1 week, moves them into long-term memory.

    Xotiradan eslash va takrorlash uzoq muddatli xotiraga o‘tkazadi.
  5. 5
    Talk together

    Real tasks where you NEED to ask and answer — like real life, not a memorised speech.

    Yodlangan matn emas, haqiqiy muloqot.
  6. 6
    Fluency: 3 rounds

    Telling the same story three times with less time (the 4-3-2 technique) makes you measurably more fluent.

    Bir hikoyani 3 marta qisqaroq vaqtda aytish ravonlikni oshiradi.
  7. 7
    Record & check

    Hearing yourself shows your mistakes. Your 1-minute challenge shows your progress.

    O‘zingizni eshitish xatolarni ko‘rsatadi, 1 daqiqalik sinov esa o‘sishni.
Best results: one unit per week · 15 minutes of audio every day · speak with a partner twice a week.

Meet Laylo’s family

Laylo is talking to Tom, a new teacher at her language centre.

  • Tom

    So, Laylo, tell me about your family. Is it big?

  • Laylo

    Quite big! There are six of us: my parents, my two brothers, my grandma and me.

  • Tom

    Wow. Are you the oldest?

  • Laylo

    No, I’m the youngest. My brothers are both older than me.

  • Tom

    What do they do?

  • Laylo

    Bekzod works as a doctor, and Jasur is still a student. He studies IT.

  • Tom

    And your parents?

  • Laylo

    My dad’s a driver and my mum’s a teacher. My grandma’s retired – she lives with us.

  • Tom

    Who do you look like?

  • Laylo

    Everyone says I look like my mum. I’m closest to her, too. What about you, Tom?

  • Tom

    Oh, I’m an only child. But I get on really well with my cousins.

  • Laylo

    That’s nice. Do you see them often?

  • Tom

    Every weekend. We usually play football together.

Sound focus: The “th” sound /ð/

Put the tip of your tongue between your teeth and use your voice. It is not “d” and not “z”.Til uchini tishlar orasiga qo‘ying va ovoz bilan ayting. Bu “d” ham, “z” ham emas.

mother · father · brother · together · they · the

“My mother and father live together with my brother.”

Remember it

Eslab qoling

Cover the English column. Read the Uzbek sentence and SAY the English aloud. Then check. Do it again tomorrow and in one week.Inglizcha ustunni yoping. O‘zbekcha gapni o‘qib, inglizchasini OVOZ chiqarib ayting va tekshiring. Ertaga va bir haftadan keyin takrorlang.

O‘zbekchaEnglish (cover!)Today · Tomorrow · Week
1Oilamizda to‘rt kishimiz.There are four of us in my family.
2Mening bitta singlim bor.I’ve got one younger sister.
3Men yolg‘iz farzandman.I’m an only child.
4Dadam haydovchi bo‘lib ishlaydi.My dad works as a driver.
5Buvim nafaqada.My grandma’s retired.
6Men dadamga o‘xshayman.I look like my dad.
7Akam juda kulgili.My brother is really funny.
8Men opam bilan yaxshi chiqishaman.I get on well with my sister.
9Ba’zan tortishamiz, lekin biz yaxshi do‘stmiz.We sometimes argue, but we’re good friends.
10Oying nima ish qiladi?What does your mum do?

Why? Remembering a phrase from memory makes it stick much better than reading it again. Iborani xotiradan eslash uni qayta o‘qishdan ko‘ra ancha yaxshi yodda saqlaydi.
